operations.comment: ; Physical $000000..$000010. Validated sixteen-byte iNES header: mapper 1, battery-backed RAM, 128 KiB PRG
; ROM and 128 KiB CHR ROM, no trainer. Preserve every header byte.
; Data; physical 16..24
; Two little-endian audio-service pointers ($8008/$8548), followed by two null cells. Header pointer
; role does not itself prove target execution.
; Consume queued sound requests, then update fades, effects, noise, music and the triangle slide. Music
; timing uses an accumulator carry stored in bit 7 of MusicTempoTick. Clear this frame's request slots after
; processing; commands may enqueue one deferred request for the next frame.
; Process each queued request before clearing the queue count.
; Start the frame with no deferred request; advance the music tempo accumulator.
; Clear six request slots, then submit the deferred request through the same priority arbitration.
; A zero or repeated request advances the current song. Request $3e resets auxiliary playback state; a
; different request initializes four music records.
; Continue playback without restarting an unchanged song.
; Start the newly selected song.
; Special reset command; tail-call the retained auxiliary-state reset implementation.
; Select a little endian list of four channel stream pointers. Four records have stride $16; clear counters
; and modulation state and set the gate mode for the first two channels.
; Load the next stream pointer and initialize this $16-byte music channel record.
; Advance to the next channel record; the four records occupy $58 bytes.
; Song $11 also clears the auxiliary triangle-effect state.
; Clear active effects and override masks; the following continuation completes the channel shutdown.
; Clear the indexed effect-state bytes before the following channel shutdown continuation.
; Finish clearing channel state, mark all four music records inactive at stride $16, and silence
; pulse/noise/triangle hardware. This continues the existing initialization loops.
; Walk four $16-byte channel records with a one-hot channel mask. Clear the current song once all four
; streams have ended.
; Update one music channel, then advance record offset, index and mask.
; Return after the channel scan or when no song is active.
; A zero stream high byte denotes an ended channel. On tempo ticks decrement gate and note counters; fetch
; commands when the note expires. Effects can own the hardware channel while music state continues to
; advance.
; The gate may already be zero; the note timer still advances.
; Keep the current note until its timer expires.
; Clear the rest flag and interpret stream events. Unless the command preserves modulation state, reset its
; cursors and request a hardware period reload.
; Persist the stream pointer after command processing; $ff in the token scratch denotes stream termination.
; Do not overwrite channels currently owned by a general effect or the dedicated noise effect.
; Return with the channel record offset in X.
; Count an inactive stream for song completion.
; Read the next music byte at Y=0. The top two bits distinguish note forms from control commands.
; Decode another event after a command has advanced Y.
; A $00..$3f event is a note using the existing gate and duration reload values.
; Advance the 16-bit stream pointer past the last consumed byte. Carry is propagated explicitly.
; A $40..$7f event carries a new gate value; bit 7 of the following byte additionally introduces a note
; duration.
; Take a seven-bit gate duration and a separate note duration.
; A $80..$bf event reuses the gate setting and supplies a new note duration.
; Values $c0..$fe select an indirect command handler using the low six bits; $ff ends the stream. The
; complete dispatch-table bounds and command vocabulary remain unresolved; do not infer arbitrary command ids.
; Data; physical 616..674
; 29 little-endian music-command targets, indices 0..28. The pointer array ends before the independent
; $8292 resume helper. Handlers consume their documented channel/stream arguments; this does not
; establish an arbitrary masked opcode domain.
; Resume the shared music stream interpreter; the bounded command pointer table ends immediately
; before this entry.
; Clear this stream pointer and count completion. Silence the hardware channel only if an effect does not
; own it; the triangle uses a different silence value.
; X is the hardware channel register stride here, restored to the record offset afterward.
; Return after terminating the stream.
; The triangle bypasses the volume envelope. For other channels, envelope bytes below $30 redirect the
; cursor; zero silences it. Other bytes combine channel control flags with volume, reduced by global and
; channel attenuation with saturation.
; Follow envelope cursor redirects until a control/volume byte or terminator is reached.
; Return without processing a volume envelope for the triangle.
; Subtract the summed attenuation high nibble from the envelope volume; clamp at zero.
; Convert the saturated attenuation to volume units.
; Preserve the upper control bits and replace only the attenuated volume nibble.
; A zero envelope byte produces pulse/noise silence control $30.
; Apply gate/rest suppression, then write the channel control and timer. A flag requests the high timer
; write that retriggers a note; clear that flag after writing.
; A rest forces the volume nibble to zero.
; Retain control flags while muting this channel.
; Triangle playback uses bit 7 of its linear counter; a closed gate or strong fade forces zero first.
; Mute the triangle before applying its linear-counter control bit.
; Apply the triangle-specific control bit.
; Convert the channel index to the APU four-register stride.
; Clear period-reload and preserve-modulation flags after this update.
; Combine note, channel transpose and global transpose, then read the period table. Optional signed
; modulation is scaled by the base period high byte; reject modulation that changes the high byte.
; Sign extend the modulation sample, shift according to the base period high byte, then add it to the period.
; Shift the signed delta into the two-byte temporary until the scale counter expires.
; Add the scaled signed delta to the base period.
; Reject a modulation result whose high byte differs from the original period.
; Return the period in the audio scratch pair.
; Select an envelope and continue decoding this stream.
; Read one attenuation byte into the current channel record and advance the stream cursor.
; Read one transpose byte into the current channel record and resume decoding.
; Set the tempo accumulator increment.
; Read a two-byte target, save the continuation in the channel record and interpret the target stream. The
; same classified block also contains return and counted-loop command handlers; this is a single saved
; return level, not a CPU-stack call.
; Clear the completion latch and resume the stream; no parameter byte is consumed.
; Select the modulation stream through a pointer table and store its enable/id byte.
; Set bit 7 of the modulation id, then resume; the companion command clears this disable bit.
; Clear bit 7 of the channel modulation id and resume.
; Set a timed rest by closing the gate and setting flag $08. The following handlers adjust transpose,
; preserve modulation, or change gate mode before resuming command decoding.
; Add the next byte to the global tempo increment, wrapping at eight bits.
; Interpret the signed parameter in sixteenths: nonnegative values subtract with a zero floor;
; negative values add their shifted low byte with an $F0 ceiling on carry. Preserve these exact
; unsigned tests.
; Queue a sound request for arbitration after all frame request slots are cleared.
; Read envelope, attenuation and transpose as three successive stream bytes.
; A=$ff resets the sound hardware; otherwise a lookup byte packs a two-bit destination slot and six-bit
; priority/id. Keep the highest request in each slot this frame.
; Clear paired request/current-id bytes while Y counts down.
; Finish clearing request/current-id and twenty fade/control bytes, then return to the request
; initializer.
; Ignore zero requests; replace a slot only when the incoming six-bit value is at least the existing request.
; Return from sound request arbitration.
; Clear the high bytes of all four general-effect stream pointers.
; A new request initializes four effect streams. Each four-byte record stores pointer, delay and last period
; high byte. Active effects override music through a one-hot mask.
; Return via stream clearing when no general effect is active.
; Load a channel stream. When delay expires, interpret either a control command below $0f or a four-byte
; hardware event.
; Continue the ordinary event path after reading its delay.
; Dispatch a low-valued effect control byte.
; Count down the channel delay.
; Advance the four-byte record and one-hot ownership mask. Clear the active effect once all four stream high
; bytes are zero.
; Return after scanning effects.
; Clear the effect stream and release its music-override bit. Mark music for a period reload when it regains
; the channel.
; Data; physical 1639..1648
; Zero-interleaved16-bit numeric offset cells including0016,002C,0042; generic lookup bytes, exact
; original subgroup layout unresolved.
; A negative delay byte selects an explicit sweep-register write.
; Read the next stream pitch, add this channel's transpose and index the little endian APU period
; table. Always write the low period; retrigger the high register with $70 only when its cached high
; period changes. Rejoin the existing effect interpreter. This 34-byte branch was fetched after an
; artificial initialized defensive-menu route; natural gameplay use is not established.
; Disable sweep and combine the event period with a signed per-channel adjustment measured in units of eight
; timer ticks.
; Propagate a positive period adjustment into the high byte. The block also handles negative adjustments by
; subtraction.
; Continue the existing relative-note branch: on borrow rewind the cursor and subtract one from the
; preceding stream byte before rejoining the common note path.
; Write the period high byte only when changed, avoiding unnecessary retriggers.
; Compare the new hardware period high byte against the cached value; skip redundant register writes
; and resume the effect event path.
; Use a little endian handler pointer indexed by twice the control byte.
; Data; physical 1784..1792
; Four little-endian effect-command targets for indices 1..4. Index zero is the preceding non-ROM
; $003E sentinel and is excluded. Loop/volume/pitch handler mechanics support these cells; higher
; selectors remain outside this contract.
; Read a deferred audio request, advance this effect stream by four bytes and resume its channel interpreter.
; Advance the effect stream pointer by the four-byte command record and resume through the shared
; stream decoder.
; A zero loop counter loads the count and computes a backward stream address in four-byte units;
; subsequent visits decrement the counter and either loop or resume after the command.
; Decrement the loop counter; repeat from the saved relative destination while nonzero.
; Add the one-byte command argument to the per-effect volume adjustment, then resume the effect
; stream.
; Add the argument to the effect pitch adjustment and resume.
; Read four little endian effect pointers and set ownership only for nonzero pointers. Initialize timer
; cache and pitch/volume adjustments. Selected effects also reset the triangle slide state.
; Clear five bytes of auxiliary triangle-effect state.
; Clear the five contiguous slide-state bytes before the stop continuation silences hardware.
; Finish clearing slide state, silence triangle output and release its channel-override bit. Continues
; the existing stop loop.
; Return from effect initialization. The following entry adjusts a hardware volume nibble with signed
; saturation; its shared clamp preserves the exact hardware nibble behavior.
; Take the low volume nibble, add the per-effect adjustment and share the signed saturation/write
; path.
; Clamp the adjusted volume to $01..$0f when outside the accepted nibble range.
; Merge the adjusted low nibble with event control flags; add the triangle linear-counter bit for channel
; offset $08.
; Set the triangle control bit before writing the channel register.
; Write the prepared control byte to the selected APU channel.
; Return when no dedicated noise effect is active.
; A request selects a dedicated noise stream and overrides music channel 3. Events are two bytes: packed
; volume/period and delay/mode. Zero terminates; one queues a deferred request.
; Continue the existing noise effect until its low-seven-bit delay expires.
; Read the next two-byte noise event through its saved pointer.
; Move the event high nibble to the period and merge the mode bit derived from the delay byte.
; Advance the dedicated noise pointer by two bytes.
; Return after advancing the noise stream.
; Decrement the dedicated noise delay.
; Release the dedicated noise override and silence the noise channel.
; Read a sound request from the next byte, then advance this stream.
; Tail-call the existing command interpreter; no new stream format is implied by this continuation.
; A request installs a signed fade mode and countdown. Negative modes raise attenuation in $10 steps to $f0;
; positive modes lower it toward zero or the saved restore target. Bit 6 of AudioControlFlags cancels the
; request.
; Clear a pending fade request; with active music also clear attenuation.
; Return from fade cancellation.
; Start the requested fade with a one-tick initial countdown.
; No new request: advance the signed fade mode when its countdown expires.
; Return while the fade waits or after it finishes.
; Increase attenuation one volume step and reload delay from the low seven mode bits.
; Lower attenuation one volume step until reaching zero or the saved target.
; Clear the fade mode.
; Stop when the saved attenuation level is reached.
